content:
Apple's MagSafe Wallet may be the top choice for most people, allowing them to store their driver's license, credit cards and a bit of cash directly on the back of their iPhone. Apple's Find My integration is indeed nice, but this convenience comes at a cost — real money, as its price is fully double that of most third-party MagSafe wallets.

Some people also don't like the material used in the MagSafe Wallet. The Urban Fit is still one of the top Apple wallet alternatives in my mind. It costs about half the price of Apple's, can hold three cards, and still works great as a MagSafe wallet.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers shares the latest news from the world of MagSafe and wireless charging, helping you get the most out of your wireless charging-compatible Apple devices.

Why choose a MagSafe wallet?

I still see the MagSafe wallet as a bridge to the future. When you can pay with Apple Pay anywhere and store your driver's license or ID directly on your iPhone, you only need to bring your phone when you leave the house. Compared to a few years ago, we are closer to this future, but until that day truly arrives, I still carry a wallet — just much thinner than before. My state has yet to announce support for digital ID.

Since jumping on the MagSafe wallet bandwagon, I now only use it, and I can't imagine going back. Having one less thing to worry about is indeed much easier. As long as it snaps on, I know my wallet and iPhone are together. As long as I have one of them, the other is definitely there.

Urban Fit Wallet Summary

  • Dimensions: 3.74 x 2.52 x 0.27 inches
  • Weight: Less than 1 ounce

Depending on the model you choose, the Urban Fit can hold two or three cards. It's made of polyurethane leather with a slightly textured, non-slip surface, so getting cards in and out is easier than with Apple's version. For me, the biggest selling point is still the flexibility in how you take out a card. You can push it up from the bottom, push it out from the back, or pull it out directly from the top — whichever is convenient. This may sound trivial, but it's actually an important part of the MagSafe wallet experience.

Overall, it still performs well, and after using it for a while I really have little to complain about. It's thin enough to hold a few cards without making your phone bulky, and it makes getting cards in and out easy. If you want a simple alternative to the Apple MagSafe wallet and don't mind giving up Find My tracking, the Urban Fit is still a good choice, costing about half the price of Apple's version.

You can buy it on Amazon.
